content.thinking: I should drop the revision mention from the root cause and just state that the deploy renamed the metrics port, keeping the rest unchanged.

action_items.item: Make the same one-line change to deploy/scrape.yaml (port `http-metrics`) on the branch that revision c3c36da was deployed from, which is not in main's history.
Deploy to io-shop a revision that carries the scrape port change.
Render the ServiceMonitor's endpoint port from `metrics.portName` in the values file so the two cannot drift apart.
Run the port-name consistency test from the draft fix as a required check on changes to the deploy/ directory.
Add an alert that fires when the io-shop ServiceMonitor selects no scrape targets.
Route MetricsAbsent alerts on io-shop to the on-call page.

causal_chain.step: Nobody using the shop saw anything wrong. Instead, the shop's metrics stopped arriving from {metrics_stopped_at}, and MetricsAbsent fired.

The metrics stopped because Prometheus had nothing to scrape. In the running revision, the ServiceMonitor selects the endpoint by the port name `metrics`, but the values file names the metrics port `http-metrics`. A name that matches no port is not an error to the operator: it gives a target list with nothing in it.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of revision 2c8f731: the shop's metrics were still being collected with it in place, up to the minute before the onset.
A feature-flag change: the flag provider shows no flag changes by anyone but Argus in the hour before it was read.

causal_chain.step: The names disagree because the deploy of revision c3c36da at {P2.1} renamed every port to the platform convention (web to http, admin to http-admin, metrics to http-metrics) in deploy/values-production.yaml. That is the only file its diff lists, so deploy/scrape.yaml still selects `metrics`. As of {T13.1}, all {T13.2} replicas ran that revision.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A planned renaming of the shop's network connection points, made to follow a platform-wide naming convention, was not carried into the separate setting that tells the monitoring system where to collect the shop's measurements, so the monitoring system found nothing to collect.

contributing_factors.factor: Nothing checks that the port name in deploy/scrape.yaml matches `metrics.portName` in deploy/values-production.yaml (the scrape file says so itself). No check of the rename against the scrape configuration was seen before the deploy.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The mismatch would have been caught before the rename reached production, and the metrics would not have stopped.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No alert was seen for the shop's ServiceMonitor selecting no scrape targets. The fault was found only by MetricsAbsent, which waits for a stretch with no samples.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The empty target list would have been flagged as soon as the deploy landed, not only after the absence window had passed.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: MetricsAbsent on io-shop did not page anyone: no on-call incident was linked to the alert.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have known straight away that the shop was unwatched and could have pushed the scrape fix through to a deploy sooner.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

got_lucky: The shop kept no metrics for the whole stretch. Had it actually broken during that time, nothing watching its metrics would have shown it or alerted on it.
went_well: Argus read the diff of the suspect deploy {T12.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, and tied the stopped metrics to the port rename.
Argus declined to roll back the rename, because undoing it would reverse a change made on purpose. It sent the incident on toward a fix instead.
Code-Fix opened a draft pull request {T20.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised. It changes the scrape's port name and adds a test that keeps the two files in step.
went_wrong: Code-Fix wrote its fix against main, which does not contain the running revision. Merging it will not bring the metrics back until a deploy carries the change, and the branch that revision c3c36da came from needs the same change before it is deployed again.

input.root_cause: The ServiceMonitor in deploy/scrape.yaml picks the endpoint to scrape by the port name `metrics`. The change renamed that port to `http-metrics` in deploy/values-production.yaml and left the scrape file alone. A ServiceMonitor port name that matches no port is not an error to the operator, so Prometheus was left with an empty target list and collected nothing from the shop.
input.still_at_risk: The scrape was still looking for a port name the running revision no longer has, so any real trouble in the shop would go unseen by anything that watches its metrics until a deploy brings the two names back into line.
input.symptom: Nobody using the shop saw anything wrong; the shop's metrics stopped arriving.
